A blessing which has brought me closer to the Sacred Heart of Christ 📿. Hallow has become one of the most meaningful parts of my daily prayer life. As someone who already had a strong faith, I am grateful for how this app has helped me maintain and deepen that faith while drawing even closer to God each day.

What has touched me most is the Rosary, especially the read-along audio for the mysteries. Hearing the mysteries read and reflected upon has helped me slow down and truly contemplate the life of Christ. Instead of simply reciting the prayers, I find myself reflecting more deeply on their meaning and understanding God’s Word with greater clarity. The guided reflections bring the mysteries to life in a way that has helped me not only understand them better, but also feel them more profoundly in my heart.

In a world that can often feel busy, distracted, and uncertain, Hallow provides a peaceful place to pause, pray, and reconnect with God. Whether you are just beginning your faith journey or have walked with the Lord for many years, this app offers something truly special. It serves as a gentle reminder that God is always present, always listening, and always inviting us to grow closer to Him.

I sincerely hope more people will consider downloading Hallow and sharing it with their loved ones. You never know how one invitation, one prayer, or one moment spent with God might change someone’s life. Even the smallest seeds of faith can grow into something beautiful. The more we share our faith, the more hearts we may inspire, helping to spread God’s love, hope, mercy, and peace throughout the world.

I wholeheartedly recommend Hallow to anyone seeking a deeper relationship with God. It has enriched my prayer life, strengthened my faith, and helped me experience the beauty of prayer in a more meaningful way. I am truly thankful for this app and the blessings it continues to bring into my life. 🙏

I am an Episcopal priest and have been enjoying several of the devotions on Hallow, including the Lent challenge in the Brothers Karamazov and the series in detachment, and the daily gospel. I also have been listening to Jeff Cavins’ daily reflection and for the most part enjoy it. 

Until today. Today (6/7/2026) Jeff was dogmatic and judgmental about the Catholic understanding of the Eucharist and said that other than the Catholic point of view all others - including Episcopal, I presume - are in error. It has become clear to me that this app’s purpose is to (a) nurture and develop the faith of Roman Catholics and (b) to convince others, including Episcopal and Orthodox Catholics (yes, Rome is not the only Catholic Church), to repent and come home to the see of Peter, which I am sure you wouldn’t hesitate to call the “one true church.” 

Jeff Cavins’ pleasant and chatty manner belies the underlying judgment he brings. Many of his reflections are helpful and uplifting but sometimes he seems to get carried away with doctrinal arrogance. Is Hallow at all interested in being useful and uplifting to any except Roman Catholics?

I will continue to make use of Hallow as one devotional aid among several, but sadly have been somewhat soured by its conservatism and exclusivist ecclesiology.
